## Ojo de Perdiz: An Overnight Stay Amid Bolivia's Desert Landscapes

[Ojo de Perdiz](/bolivia/place/ojo-de-perdiz/) (also known as Ojito de Perdiz) lies in a high-altitude region of southwestern [Bolivia](/bolivia/), near the [Siloli Desert](/bolivia/place/siloli-desert/). On itineraries between [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), the Altiplano lagoons, and protected natural areas, it serves primarily as **a rest and overnight stop**, allowing travelers to divide a long road journey into several days.

The landscape is quite different from postcard images of Uyuni: instead of uninterrupted white salt, there are stony plains, low desert slopes, dry air, a long dirt road, and sparse vegetation. Familiar urban infrastructure is limited. Travelers come for the Altiplano journey itself, rather than city attractions.

## Where Is Ojo de Perdiz, and Why Do Travelers Stop Here?

The name Ojo de Perdiz is associated with a local water source and partridge-like birds, as explained by Hotel Tayka del Desierto in the area. The region lies near the Siloli Desert at approximately 4,500 meters above sea level. Actual elevation varies with the specific stopping point, but this is demanding high-altitude terrain in any case.

Travel from [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) follows routes through southern highland landscapes and lagoons. Parts of the roads are unpaved, and the map distance gives little indication of the travel time. Four-wheel-drive vehicles are usually used, with timing subject to road and weather conditions.

Accommodation around Ojo de Perdiz allows a night between two busy days. The route may pass [Laguna Hedionda](/bolivia/place/laguna-hedionda/), other flamingo lagoons, and natural sites closer to Chile. This is a geographically logical sequence, but the precise stops must be checked against the selected tour.

## What Can You See Along the Way?

For most travelers, Ojo de Perdiz is important as part of a continuous change of landscapes. To the north lie salt plains and volcanic mountains; farther along the road are mineral-rich lagoons, deserts, and rock formations.

On the [14-day Grand Tour of South America: Peru, Bolivia and Chile](/multi-country/tour/south-america-peru-bolivia-chile-easter-island/), **Day 10** crosses the Altiplano toward Ojo de Perdiz. The route includes Hedionda, Honda, Cañapa, and Ramaditas lagoons; by evening, the group arrives in the Ojo de Perdiz area for dinner and an overnight stay. Flamingos inhabit the lagoon region, but their locations and numbers change in the wild.

On **Day 11**, the journey continues to [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), the [Sol de Mañana geyser field](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/), [Chalviri Lagoon](/bolivia/place/laguna-chalviri/), and [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), before crossing into Chile. This creates a useful division: one day for driving and several lagoons, the next for southern natural sites and the border crossing.

**Important when choosing a tour:** the name Ojo de Perdiz alone does not imply a separate excursion, guarantee a particular hotel, or confirm visits to every nearby lagoon. These details are established by the itinerary and conditions of the specific trip.

## Preparing for a Night in the High-Altitude Desert

The greatest difference from an ordinary city hotel is the elevation and remoteness. Nights can be extremely cold even after a sunny day. Wind intensifies the cold, while physical activity that normally feels easy can become more demanding at altitude.

| What to Consider | Practical Preparation |
|---|---|
| Around 4,500 m elevation | Plan acclimatization in advance |
| Cold and wind | Warm layers and head protection |
| Long drives | Water, snacks, and time buffer |
| Remote location | Confirm overnight facilities beforehand |

Altitude sickness can affect physically fit travelers too. Ascend gradually, avoid strenuous activity immediately after a sharp gain in elevation, and discuss the journey with a physician beforehand if you have relevant risk factors. With serious symptoms, do not keep ascending in the hope that they will resolve on their own.

Because the area is remote from major settlements, ask the organizer how transport, meals, electricity, and communications work at the actual accommodation. Do not assume mobile internet and hotel services will match those in La Paz or Uyuni. An individual hotel may have Wi-Fi or heating, but those amenities cannot be assumed for the whole region.

## Ojo de Perdiz Versus the Siloli Desert

The [Siloli Desert](/bolivia/place/siloli-desert/) is an extensive natural area known for wind-shaped and volcanic landscapes. Ojo de Perdiz is a specific stop on the high-altitude route near it. A traveler may stay overnight at Ojo de Perdiz while spending most sightseeing time at lagoons and other Siloli sites.

The [Stone Tree](/bolivia/place/arbol-de-piedra/) also features on routes through this region, but it is a separate rock formation. If seeing a particular rock shape or photographing a lagoon is essential, look for that named stop in the itinerary rather than relying on the general term “Siloli.”

For a complete trip, compare [Bolivia tours](/bolivia/tour/) and specific options in the [multi-country travel catalog](/multi-country/).

## When Is the Best Time to Go?

Altiplano routes operate during different parts of the year, but conditions vary substantially. Southern Hemisphere summer rains can complicate travel on certain roads; drier periods generally bring less precipitation but also colder nights. Wind and sudden temperature changes are possible at altitude in any season.

If continuing to Chile, coordinate the border-crossing time and allow for possible delays. In such a remote area, an itinerary with an experienced driver, suitable vehicle, and confirmed overnight stop makes much more sense than attempting to travel between natural sites unprepared.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Ojo de Perdiz

### Is Ojo de Perdiz a town or a natural attraction?

It is a remote high-altitude area and stopping point on routes through the Siloli Desert. Travelers visit it mainly between natural sights of the Altiplano.

### Can I See Flamingos Right Beside the Hotel?

Flamingos inhabit certain lagoons in southwestern Bolivia, including areas along the route to Ojo de Perdiz. Sightings depend on the particular lake, season, and movements of the birds; an encounter beside the hotel cannot be guaranteed.

### Is Ojo de Perdiz Included in Ada Tours Trips?

Yes. The [14-day journey through Peru, Bolivia and Chile](/multi-country/tour/south-america-peru-bolivia-chile-easter-island/) arrives at Ojo de Perdiz for dinner and an overnight stay on **Day 10**.

### Why Is Preparation for Altitude Necessary?

The area lies around 4,500 meters above sea level. Less oxygen is available at this elevation, while cold and exertion add to the demands on the body. Plan acclimatization before the trip.

## Tours Through Ojo de Perdiz in Bolivia: What's Included?

[Ojo de Perdiz](/bolivia/place/ojo-de-perdiz/) lies in the high-altitude southwest of Bolivia near the [Siloli Desert](/bolivia/place/siloli-desert/). On Altiplano journeys, it is a landmark between [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and the natural areas of colored lagoons, eroded rocks, and geothermal fields. A standalone city sightseeing excursion would make little sense here: the area is normally visited on multi-day highland routes.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Ojo de Perdiz on the main route. These include a 14-day journey through Peru, Bolivia and Chile, a 15-day itinerary covering Altiplano lakes, and a grand private 33-day route through South America. The main difference is **how much time is devoted to southwestern Bolivia and whether an overnight stay is included**.

## Where Is Ojo de Perdiz Relative to Uyuni and the Lagoons?

After Uyuni's white surface, the road crosses dry high-altitude plains. The landscape grows stonier, settlements become fewer, and unpaved stretches pass volcanic slopes. Major natural landmarks farther along include [Laguna Hedionda](/bolivia/place/laguna-hedionda/), [Laguna Cañapa](/bolivia/place/laguna-canapa/), and other Altiplano lakes. Flamingos can sometimes be seen around these lagoons.

The later excursion may include the [Stone Tree](/bolivia/place/arbol-de-piedra/) in Siloli, [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) in the [Eduardo Avaroa Reserve](/bolivia/place/eduardo-avaroa-national-reserve/), the [Sol de Mañana geysers](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/), and [Polques Hot Springs](/bolivia/place/polques-hot-springs/). Some programs end near [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/) before continuing into Chile.

These sites lie far apart. Ojo de Perdiz therefore matters for logistics as well: an overnight stop divides a long high-altitude transfer into manageable sections. The [Ojo de Perdiz destination guide](/bolivia/place/ojo-de-perdiz/) explains its place within Altiplano geography in more detail.

## Comparing Itineraries Featuring Ojo de Perdiz

| Tour | Distinctive Feature |
|---|---|
| [Peru, Bolivia and Chile: 14 Days](/multi-country/tour/south-america-peru-bolivia-chile-easter-island/) | Lagoons and an overnight stay at Ojo de Perdiz |
| [Peru and Bolivia: 15 Days](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-lakes-15-days/) | Uyuni, an overnight stop, then Eduardo Avaroa |
| [Grand Private Tour: 33 Days](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/) | A high-altitude stage en route from Bolivia into Chile |

### A 14-Day Route: Through the Highlands Toward Atacama

The [14-day grand tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-peru-bolivia-chile-easter-island/) begins with sights in Peru, Lake Titicaca, and La Paz, followed by Uyuni. On Day 10, the route reaches Ojo de Perdiz via high-altitude lagoons. The itinerary explicitly includes lunch along the road, dinner, and an overnight stay in the area. The following day features Laguna Colorada, Sol de Mañana, and the road to San Pedro de Atacama. This suits travelers who want to see **the Peruvian Andes, Bolivian lagoons, and the Chilean desert** on one journey.

### A 15-Day Route: More Time for Uyuni and the Altiplano

[Peru and Bolivia with Altiplano Lakes](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-lakes-15-days/) connects Machu Picchu, Titicaca, and La Paz with Uyuni Salt Flat. It then continues to San Cristóbal, high-altitude rock landscapes, and Ojo de Perdiz. **An overnight stay is planned, but the specific hotel and category are confirmed for the chosen program.** Siloli, Laguna Colorada, geysers, and springs follow on the next day. Before payment, check the onward transfer and the overnight accommodation after that long day, as the itinerary itself contains relevant clarifications.

### A 33-Day Grand Journey: Ojo de Perdiz on the Cross-Border Route

The [33-day private South America tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/) starts in Peru, crosses Bolivia and Chile, and then continues to other parts of the continent. In Bolivia, a day visiting high-altitude lagoons and heading toward Atacama follows Uyuni. Ojo de Perdiz appears among the stops on this leg. **The term VIP in a tour title does not confirm a particular vehicle or hotel class on this specific section:** compare stated services and conditions, not merely a catalog category.

## What to Check When Choosing a Highland Tour

Unlike sightseeing in [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) or a short visit to Uyuni, the southern Altiplano involves long road journeys. Four practical questions matter:

- **Overnight stay:** Is accommodation at Ojo de Perdiz listed, and is the hotel named? If not, confirm the lodging before payment.
- **Direction of travel:** Does the natural route start at Uyuni and finish on the Chilean side, or return to Bolivia?
- **Stops:** How much time is allocated to [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), and [Sol de Mañana](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/)?
- **Altitude and roads:** Are there long dirt-road stretches, early starts, and breaks for rest?

The Siloli region lies high in the Andes. Water, sunscreen, warm clothing, and shoes suitable for stony stopping points are helpful even in a warmer season. Altitude affects physical tolerance, especially after arriving from lowland cities. Do not approach this stage as if it were a normal city stroll; travelers with conditions affected by elevation should discuss the trip with a doctor in advance.

## When to Plan a Trip Through Ojo de Perdiz

Drier months in southwestern Bolivia are generally more convenient for driving on unpaved roads and visiting high-altitude natural sites. However, nights on the plateau are cold, and winds intensify the chill. During wetter periods, the route may need to change on some stretches.

If the trip includes Uyuni, the season also affects the salt flat's appearance. Reflections of clouds in the water attract visitors during rainy months, whereas the dry surface reveals distinct salt patterns. **Salt-flat conditions and access to remote roads must be assessed separately:** good weather in La Paz does not mean similar conditions in Siloli.

For a broader choice of the country's nature routes, explore [Bolivia tours](/bolivia/tour/) and [nature and wildlife tours in Bolivia](/interests/wildlife/tours/bolivia/). These help compare the southern highlands with very different regions of the country.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Ojo de Perdiz Tours

### Are Ojo de Perdiz and the “Eyes of Water” on Uyuni the Same Place?

No. [Ojo de Perdiz](/bolivia/place/ojo-de-perdiz/) is a high-altitude stop near Siloli, whereas the [“Eyes of Water”](/bolivia/place/ojos-del-salar/) are small openings filled with water on Uyuni Salt Flat. A similar Spanish word in their names refers to completely different locations. There is a [separate tour selection for the Eyes of Water](/bolivia/place/ojos-del-salar/tour/).

### Does Every Tour Include an Overnight Stay at Ojo de Perdiz?

No. The 14-day and 15-day itineraries explicitly include accommodation in the Ojo de Perdiz area; on other routes it may simply be a point on the way to the lagoons and the Chilean border. The actual hotel, category, and order of nights depend on the chosen tour.

### Can I Visit Ojo de Perdiz on a Day Trip from Uyuni?

On our tours, it is part of a multi-day high-altitude stage. The great distances, dirt roads, and several natural stops make a simple out-and-back day trip an unsuitable substitute for the complete route.

### How Does a Tour Through Ojo de Perdiz Differ from a Regular Salt-Flat Excursion?

Check whether the day-by-day journey goes **beyond Uyuni toward the lagoons, Siloli, and the Eduardo Avaroa Reserve**. If only [Colchani](/bolivia/place/colchani/), [Incahuasi](/bolivia/place/incahuasi-island/), and the salt surface are listed, the excursion serves a different purpose.

## The Eyes of Water on Uyuni: What's Beneath the White Salt Surface?

The [Eyes of Water](/bolivia/place/ojos-del-salar/) are natural water-filled holes and hollows in the salt crust of [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). Against the vast white plain, they appear as small dark or bluish patches. They reveal that a salt flat is a complex natural formation: beneath the seemingly solid surface lie layers of salt, water, and brine.

This stop offers a different experience from typical photographs of mirror-like Uyuni. In the rainy season, reflections form where water spreads over large stretches of the surface. The Eyes of Water allow visitors to observe small localized openings and cavities **without trying to photograph a continuous mirror of the sky**.

## How Do Holes Form in the Salt Crust?

Uyuni Salt Flat formed in an enclosed high-altitude basin where ancient lakes changed over time and their water evaporated, leaving salts behind. Brine remains within the salt deposits. Its movement, the dissolution of salt, and localized cavities can create holes in the surface.

In tourism descriptions, these openings are called *Ojos del Salar*, *Ojos de Sal*, or “eyes of salt.” The visible size of an opening does not indicate the depth of the space below. Geological studies describe areas of the salt flat where a small surface opening connects to a wider cavity filled with brine.

For this reason, **do not walk on the edge of an unfamiliar opening or taste the water**. Observe from a safe distance, following the guide's instructions.

## Where Do the Eyes of Water Fit into the Uyuni Route?

Trips across the salt flat often combine the natural water openings with [Colchani](/bolivia/place/colchani/), where visitors learn about salt extraction and processing, and [Incahuasi Island](/bolivia/place/incahuasi-island/), known for cacti and panoramic viewpoints. These stops serve different purposes: salt production, water processes inside the salt flat, and broad views over the white plain.

On Ada Tours' [3-day four-wheel-drive tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-salt-flats-jeep-tour-3-days/), the Eyes of Water feature on Day 3. After an early departure onto the salt flat, the itinerary includes Colchani, this geological stop, and Incahuasi Island. It ends in Uyuni, with a transfer to San Pedro de Atacama available for the option finishing in Chile.

On the [11-day Bolivia itinerary](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-titicaca-uyuni-la-paz-11-days/), Ojos del Salar features on the Uyuni day between Colchani and the onward route to the island. This is part of a larger journey through Titicaca, La Paz, lagoons, and Torotoro.

## How Do the Eyes of Water Differ from Salt Patterns?

In the dry season, polygonal salt cells are often visible on Uyuni's surface. These crust patterns form through interactions between salt, moisture, and drying. The individual water openings, by contrast, are local breaks in the crust where water or brine is exposed.

| What You See | Natural Feature |
|---|---|
| White polygons | Salt-crust patterns |
| Water-filled opening | Local exposure of water and brine |
| Mirror-like surface | A thin layer of water after rainfall |

Several surface forms may occur during one journey, but their appearance depends on the season and exact area of the salt flat.

## When to Go and How to Behave at the Site

During the dry season, much of the accessible route usually crosses firm salt. During rainy periods, water can cover wide stretches and produce reflections, but also restrict vehicle access. The possibility of stopping at a particular opening and approaching it depends on road conditions and the guide's decision.

Sunlight is extremely bright on the white high-altitude surface. Bring UV-protective sunglasses, a hat, water, and appropriate shoes. The salt flat lies high in the Andes, so acclimatization matters. Do not try to test the depth of an opening with your foot or leave objects in the water.

## How to Choose a Tour Including This Stop

If geology interests you, compare the sequence of [Colchani](/bolivia/place/colchani/), the Eyes of Water, [Incahuasi](/bolivia/place/incahuasi-island/), and other Uyuni sights. Merely mentioning the salt flat does not confirm that every one is included. On longer multi-country journeys, time at Uyuni may be considerably shorter than on a dedicated four-wheel-drive expedition.

We can help compare confirmed stops and transport formats to choose a route for photography, geology, or a broader journey through the Altiplano.

## Frequently Asked Questions About the Eyes of Water

### Are the Eyes of Water Geysers?

No. These are small holes and water openings in the salt crust, not the hot geothermal fields of [Sol de Mañana](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/).

### Can I Drink the Water?

No. It may contain high concentrations of dissolved salts; these visitor sites are not sources of drinking water.

### Do the Eyes of Water Exist Only During the Rainy Season?

The underlying salt-crust structure and brine cavities are distinct from the seasonal mirror effect. However, visibility and access to a specific opening depend on water levels and surface conditions.

### Do I Need to Walk Across the Salt Flat to Reach Them?

Tours normally stop during a vehicle journey. The guide determines the actual walking distance and the safe observation point.

## Tours to the Eyes of Water on Uyuni Salt Flat

The [Eyes of Water](/bolivia/place/ojos-del-salar/) are natural water-filled openings in the salt surface of [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). Against the endless white plain, they appear as small dark or bluish patches. A stop allows visitors to observe the salt crust and water inside the hollows. It is one way to discover the salt flat in detail rather than only from a viewpoint.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Ojos del Salar on the main route. For some travelers, this is one part of a short four-wheel-drive tour of southwestern Bolivia; for others, it is a brief episode on a journey across several countries. **The Eyes of Water rarely take up an entire sightseeing day:** most time goes to driving across the salt flat, visiting other sites, and reaching accommodation.

## What Exactly Will You See at Ojos del Salar?

Uyuni is a vast salt plain on Bolivia's Altiplano. The white crust preserves traces of water and salt movement, with mineral-rich water emerging at individual points. These small exposed areas are known as the Eyes of Water. They differ from the broad high-altitude lagoons found farther south in Bolivia.

The [Eyes of Water destination page](/bolivia/place/ojos-del-salar/) describes the feature in greater detail. On an itinerary, it is often more interesting to follow the succession of landscapes: [Colchani](/bolivia/place/colchani/) and its salt industry, Uyuni's open surface, the water openings, and [Incahuasi Island](/bolivia/place/incahuasi-island/) with tall cacti.

These stops have distinct purposes. Colchani introduces salt processing, Incahuasi offers views from a rocky rise, and the Eyes of Water reveal small patches of exposed water within the white crust. Seeing them together is useful if you want to understand Uyuni close up.

### A 3-Day Four-Wheel-Drive Tour: Salt Flat and Lagoons

The [3-day Uyuni excursion](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-salt-flats-jeep-tour-3-days/) covers far more than the white salt plain. The itinerary begins with [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), the [Sol de Mañana geysers](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/), and [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), followed by high-altitude lagoons and volcanic landscapes. The Eyes of Water appear on Day 3, together with Colchani and Incahuasi.

Choose this option if you want to see **both the multicolored lakes of southwestern Bolivia and the salt flat** in just a few days. It crosses several remote natural regions rather than spending three days solely on the salt surface. Check the tour listing for the exact start and finish points, included meals, and overnight stays.

### Bolivia in 11 Days: Add Cities and Titicaca

The [Bolivia in 11 Days itinerary](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-titicaca-uyuni-la-paz-11-days/) combines [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/), [Lake Titicaca](/bolivia/place/lake-titicaca-bolivia/), Uyuni, southern lagoons, and Torotoro. Compared with the short four-wheel-drive tour, it offers more geographical variety within Bolivia but requires more transfers. The Eyes of Water are one stop during the introduction to the salt flat.

If you are interested in Bolivian culture and nature on the same journey, assess this option by the distribution of nights between cities and highlands. Uyuni is only one part of the busy schedule.

### Peru and Bolivia: Combining Uyuni with Machu Picchu

The [12-day group itinerary](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-12-days/) goes from Lima and Cusco to Machu Picchu, Lake Titicaca, and the Bolivian salt flat. On the Uyuni day, the itinerary includes Colchani, the salt fields, Ojos del Salar, and Incahuasi. It combines Peruvian archaeology with Bolivian natural landscapes rather than focusing on a multi-day expedition through the Siloli Desert.

The [15-day journey with Altiplano lakes](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-lakes-15-days/) extends the Peruvian section with further travel from Uyuni to high-altitude lagoons. After the salt flat come [Ojo de Perdiz](/bolivia/place/ojo-de-perdiz/), the [Siloli Desert](/bolivia/place/siloli-desert/), and protected natural areas. It suits travelers who want to spend more time on Bolivian landscapes while keeping Machu Picchu and Titicaca in the itinerary.

### Five Countries on One Journey

The [18-day five-country group tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) connects Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Bolivia, and Peru. Uyuni and the Eyes of Water are part of a broad journey, with its duration and transfers divided across several borders and attractions. The [Rio Carnival tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/) has an additional event-oriented purpose, so choosing it solely for Uyuni would be an unusual decision.

If the salt flat is your main reason for traveling, first compare [Bolivia tours](/bolivia/tour/) and options with a longer Bolivian section. If you want an overview of several countries, a longer itinerary may be a better fit.

## How Seasons Change the Uyuni Experience

Two very different types of scenery may be seen on the salt flat.

**During relatively dry months**, the white salt surface and polygonal patterns are exposed. The water in individual Eyes of Water openings stands out against the salt. Under suitable conditions, vehicle routes can cover areas that are inaccessible in the wet season.

**During the rainy period**, most often around December to March, parts of the flat are covered with a thin layer of water, creating a mirrored surface. This famous natural phenomenon depends on precipitation, wind, and location. Flooding can change access to [Incahuasi](/bolivia/place/incahuasi-island/) and some other stops; the Eyes of Water also look different from the dry season.

No month guarantees perfect reflections or access to every site. Choose according to the experience you most want, then check current conditions and the order of stops on the sightseeing day.

## What to Consider Before Traveling

Uyuni lies around 3,600 meters above sea level. The plateau can affect travelers who have recently arrived from lowlands. Bring sunglasses, sunscreen, drinking water, a warm layer, and comfortable shoes. Water in natural openings on the salt flat is neither drinking water nor a place for swimming.

The salt crust is uneven in places. Near exposed water, stay on the route shown by your guide rather than testing the strength of the edge yourself. On sunny days, glare from the white surface can be strong even when the air is cool.

If the journey continues toward [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) and the [Eduardo Avaroa Reserve](/bolivia/place/eduardo-avaroa-national-reserve/), clothing and driving-time requirements become more demanding. This is a separate high-altitude stage with dirt roads and more remote accommodation.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Tours to the Eyes of Water

### Are the Eyes of Water and Ojo de Perdiz the Same Place?

No. The [Eyes of Water](/bolivia/place/ojos-del-salar/) are on Uyuni Salt Flat. [Ojo de Perdiz](/bolivia/place/ojo-de-perdiz/) is an area near the Siloli Desert along a more distant Altiplano route, with its [own tour catalog](/bolivia/place/ojo-de-perdiz/tour/).

### Do the Eyes of Water Need a Separate Day?

Usually not. On current itineraries, this is a brief stop within a visit to Uyuni, alongside Colchani, salt landscapes, and other natural sites. Sufficient time for the whole salt flat matters more.

### Does the Three-Day Four-Wheel-Drive Tour Include the Eyes of Water?

Yes. On Ada Tours' [three-day four-wheel-drive tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-salt-flats-jeep-tour-3-days/), the Eyes of Water are scheduled for Day 3. The program also covers lagoons and geothermal areas before reaching the salt flat.

### Can I See Both the Eyes of Water and High-Altitude Lagoons on One Trip?

## Ollagüe Volcano in Bolivia: The Chilean Border, Altiplano, and Routes from Uyuni

[Ollagüe Volcano](/bolivia/place/ollague-volcano/) lies on the national border between Bolivia and Chile. It is a large stratovolcano of the Central Andes, reaching 5,868 meters above sea level according to the Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program. Its rocky slopes rise over the dry Altiplano plains, where roads pass between salt flats, volcanic massifs, and lakes.

**On most sightseeing routes, Ollagüe is a natural landmark viewed from the road or a designated viewpoint.** Driving past the volcano and climbing to its summit are completely different forms of travel. A route that merely passes through the Ollagüe area should not be mistaken for an ascent.

## Where Is Ollagüe, and Why Does It Stand Out?

Ollagüe lies on the border between Chile's Antofagasta Region and the Bolivian highlands. Nearby are mountain valleys, dry salt flats, and cross-border transport links. But **a view of a border volcano does not mean travelers actually cross the border**: a crossing requires a separate route, an operating checkpoint, and the necessary documents.

Ollagüe's slopes include dark volcanic rock, dry scree, and patches of pale deposits. In clear weather the massif can be seen from far away, with almost vegetation-free expanses between the road and summit.

Ollagüe belongs to the Andean volcanic arc. Its geological history involves prolonged accumulation of lava and pyroclastic rocks. The Smithsonian reports fumarolic activity near the summit, where hot gases and steam escape from parts of the volcano. This confirms geological activity in the area but **does not mean visitors will necessarily see smoke or be able to approach the crater**.

## What Landscapes Surround the Volcano?

### Chiguana Salt Flat

[Chiguana](/bolivia/place/chiguana-salt-flat/) lies in the southwestern Bolivian highlands. Unlike Uyuni's enormous white surface, the landscape here consists of dry plains, stony terrain, mountain ranges, and volcanoes on the horizon. Some tours include views of Ollagüe while crossing this area.

### High-Altitude Lagoons

Farther south, road routes may continue to [Laguna Honda](/bolivia/place/laguna-honda/), [Laguna Hedionda](/bolivia/place/laguna-hedionda/), and [Laguna Cañapa](/bolivia/place/laguna-canapa/). The landscape changes as water appears amid mineral deposits, surrounded by other volcanic massifs. Sightings of flamingos and other birds depend on the season and natural conditions.

The southern part of the route contains [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), the Siloli Desert, and the geothermal areas of the Eduardo Avaroa Reserve. These are not immediately on Ollagüe's slopes, so they require separate travel and additional time.

### How Is Ollagüe Different from Tunupa?

Both volcanoes are associated with the Uyuni region but lie in different areas and play different roles in a journey.

| Place | Position on the Route |
|---|---|
| [Tunupa](/bolivia/place/tunupa-volcano/) | Northern part of Uyuni Salt Flat |
| [Ollagüe](/bolivia/place/ollague-volcano/) | Border areas of Bolivia and Chile |
| [Chiguana](/bolivia/place/chiguana-salt-flat/) | Southwestern salt plains |
| [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) | Distant southern highlands |

To see both volcanoes, plan a route through different parts of the Altiplano. The general phrase “trip to Uyuni” does not guarantee a visit to either Ollagüe or Tunupa.

## How Do Travelers Visit Ollagüe?

Most sightseeing journeys in this volcanic region use four-wheel-drive vehicles. The highlands have long distances between settlements, dirt roads, and sudden weather changes. Fuel reserves, water, communications, an experienced driver, and realistic timing between overnight stops are important.

Altitude also deserves attention. Strong winds, nighttime frost, and intense daytime sunshine are possible on the plateau and mountain passes. Reducing exertion and acclimatizing gradually are particularly important for travelers unfamiliar with high-altitude journeys.

For photographs, stop at a permitted safe viewpoint. Do not drive off established roads to get closer to the slopes: loose ground, remoteness, and the border zone make unauthorized detours risky.

On the [three-day Uyuni four-wheel-drive tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-salt-flats-jeep-tour-3-days/), the Ollagüe Volcano area features on Day 2 after the high-altitude lagoons and Siloli Desert, before the route continues toward Puerto Chuvica. This itinerary crosses several natural zones, with views of the volcano as one stage of the road expedition.

On the [Peru and Bolivia: Uyuni and Altiplano Lakes tour](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-lakes-15-days/), the volcano area also features on the route across the southern Altiplano, linked with a journey via San Cristóbal, rocky valleys, and high-altitude lagoons. In both cases, check the exact stops, duration, and guiding arrangements in the specific itinerary.

**Visiting the volcano area on a route does not mean an organized ascent.** Climbing an active volcano would require separate specialist planning, an assessment of volcanic conditions, and mountaineering preparation; standard sightseeing itineraries do not promise this.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Ollagüe Volcano

### Where Is Ollagüe Volcano?

On the Bolivia–Chile border in the high Central Andes. Road itineraries normally treat it as a landmark between [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), [Chiguana](/bolivia/place/chiguana-salt-flat/), and the southern lagoons.

### How Tall Is Ollagüe?

The Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program gives an elevation of approximately 5,868 meters above sea level. This is the summit altitude, not necessarily the altitude of the road used by travelers.

### Is Ollagüe an Active Volcano?

Fumarolic activity has been observed. The Smithsonian's geological profile contains no confirmed historical series of eruptions but describes hot gas vents near the summit. Current route safety should be assessed using updates from the relevant authorities.

### Can I See Ollagüe on a Three-Day Uyuni Tour?

Yes. It is included on Ada Tours' [three-day itinerary](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-salt-flats-jeep-tour-3-days/). Whether the summit is visible depends on the weather, and the itinerary means sightseeing in the area rather than a guaranteed climb.
